dimensions.note: Datasheet gives a 3.0 mm minimum for the flat negative contact.

geometry.note: Tab color is stated on the Energizer datasheet and matches the Wikipedia size list. Retail and brand pages say the colors are the same across manufacturers, but no standards document that sets them was found.

capacity_mah.conditions: Power One p13: IEC hearing aid standard test to 1.05 V (3 mA base load, 12 mA 100 ms pulse every 2 h), 20 °C, 55% RH; 300 mAh under the IEC wireless streaming test to 1.1 V

variants.notes: Rayovac rates 149 h in a hearing aid test (2 mA background, 6 mA pulse) and 89 h in the IEC standard test to 1.05 V at 21 °C.

interchange.note: A 312 is the same 7.9 mm across but 3.6 mm tall instead of 5.4 mm, and it holds less. A 13 does not fit a 312 compartment. Phonak makes the same hearing aid in a 312 model and a 13 model, and tells owners to find the right size from the marking inside the battery door.

safety: Swallowed or inserted button batteries can cause severe burns within hours. If a battery may have been swallowed or placed in the nose or ear, call the National Battery Ingestion Hotline at 1-800-498-8666 or a poison center at 1-800-222-1222 immediately, and do not wait for symptoms.
Keep hearing aid batteries out of reach of children and pets, and check the battery compartment is closed; a battery that looks like a pill can be swallowed by an adult.
notes: Remove the plastic tab covering the air holes and let the battery stand about one minute before inserting, so the battery can activate (Rayovac data sheet). The battery starts consuming zinc once the tab is removed, and an unused battery is guaranteed four years only with the tab applied. Zinc-air batteries draw oxygen through the air holes in the positive can, so output voltage and service life depend on how much air reaches the battery; Rayovac describes an air management system that meters air to high-drain devices.
